items.title: Customer feedback widget
items.descriptionMd:
Let customers send feedback from inside any page of their own product, and let our users triage it in one inbox.

## Outcomes

- A widget a customer can embed with one `<script>` tag.
- An inbox that groups, filters and assigns feedback.
- An export so teams can take their feedback elsewhere.

items.title: Accounts and sign-in
items.descriptionMd: Everything a person needs to get into Harbor and stay in safely: password sign-in, single sign-on for larger teams, and a password reset that works.

items.title: Billing and plans
items.descriptionMd: Self-serve plans, invoices and seat-based pricing, so a team can start paying without talking to us.

items.title: Embeddable feedback widget
items.descriptionMd:
As a customer of a Harbor user, I can open a small panel on their site and send a message with an optional screenshot.

### Acceptance

- Loads with one script tag:

```html
<script src="https://widget.example.invalid/harbor.js" data-project="demo" async></script>
```

- Works on mobile widths down to 320 px.
- Never blocks the host page from loading.

comments.body: First cut is up behind a flag. The panel opens in **180 ms** on a mid-range phone.
Nice. Can we keep the launcher button out of the way of cookie banners? See the bug I just filed.

Bundle size check:

- `harbor.js`: 21 kB gzipped
- budget: 25 kB

We're fine for now.

items.title: Feedback inbox with triage
items.descriptionMd: One list of every piece of feedback, newest first, with filters for status, source page and label. A teammate can assign an item or mark it done without opening it.

items.title: Export feedback as CSV
items.descriptionMd:
Teams want to take feedback into a spreadsheet or another tool. Add an **Export** button to the inbox that downloads every item matching the current filters as a CSV file.

Columns: date, author email, page, message, labels, status.

items.title: 反馈组件支持简体中文
items.descriptionMd:
## 背景

我们在亚洲的客户越来越多，很多团队希望反馈组件能直接显示中文。目前组件里的按钮、提示和错误信息都只有英文。

## 目标

- 组件根据页面的 `lang` 属性自动选择简体中文或英文。
- 所有文案都放在翻译文件里，不再写死在代码中。
- 中文文案由母语者审校后再上线。

## 不在本次范围内

繁体中文和日文会在下一个版本中处理。

items.title: Sign in with email and password
items.descriptionMd:
A person can create an account and sign in with an email address and a password. Sessions last 30 days on a trusted device.

See the [password storage guidelines](https://docs.example.invalid/security/passwords) for the hashing parameters.

comments.body: All three subtasks are merged. Running a last check on staging.

items.title: Single sign-on with SAML
items.descriptionMd: Larger customers need their people to sign in through their own identity provider. Support SAML 2.0 with one identity provider per workspace.

items.title: Reset a forgotten password
items.descriptionMd: A person who forgot their password can ask for a reset link by email and choose a new password. The link works once and expires after one hour.

items.title: Choose a plan
items.descriptionMd: A pricing page inside the app that compares the three plans and lets an owner switch between them.

items.title: Invoice history
items.descriptionMd: Owners can see every invoice for their workspace, newest first, and download each one as a PDF.

items.title: Bill by seat
items.descriptionMd: Charge per active member each month instead of a flat price. A member counts as active if they signed in during the billing period.

items.title: Render the widget panel inside a shadow root
items.descriptionMd: Keep the host page's CSS from leaking into the panel, and ours from leaking out.

items.title: Rate-limit widget submissions
items.descriptionMd: At most 10 messages per minute per visitor. Return `429` with a `Retry-After` header when the limit is hit.

items.title: Inbox list with filters
items.descriptionMd: Status, page and label filters, kept in the URL so a filtered view can be shared.

comments.body: I can take this one. Should the label filter be AND or OR?
OR, the same as the issue list. Thanks!

items.title: Assign several feedback items at once
items.descriptionMd: Select items with checkboxes and pick an assignee from a menu. One request, not one per item.

items.title: Write the CSV export as UTF-8 with a byte-order mark
items.descriptionMd: Spreadsheet apps guess the encoding of a CSV file. A byte-order mark at the start makes them read names with accents and emoji correctly.

items.title: Escape spreadsheet formulas in CSV cells
items.descriptionMd: A cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` can run as a formula when the file is opened. Prefix such cells with a single quote.

items.title: 翻译反馈组件文案
items.descriptionMd:
把反馈组件里的全部文案整理成一个翻译文件，并补齐简体中文版本：

1. 按钮：「发送反馈」「取消」
2. 提示：「谢谢你的反馈！」
3. 错误：「发送失败，请稍后再试。」

完成后请在 `zh-CN` 页面上截图确认排版没有问题。

items.title: Hash passwords with Argon2id
items.descriptionMd: Use Argon2id with the parameters from the guidelines. Re-hash on sign-in when the stored parameters are older.

items.title: Lock an account after repeated failed sign-ins
items.descriptionMd: After 10 failed attempts in 15 minutes, lock sign-in for 15 minutes and email the account owner.

items.title: Validate SAML assertions
items.descriptionMd: Check the signature, the audience, the issuer and the time window of every assertion. Reject anything unsigned.

comments.body:
Worth reading before starting: the usual mistakes are

1. trusting the first `Assertion` element
2. not checking `NotOnOrAfter`
3. accepting a comment inside the `NameID`
Noted. I'll use the library's strict mode and add a test per item.

items.title: Upload identity provider metadata
items.descriptionMd: An owner uploads the provider's XML metadata file; we read the certificate and the sign-in URL from it.

items.title: Password reset email
items.descriptionMd: A short plain email with one link. The link carries a single-use token, never the email address.

items.title: Expire reset tokens after one hour
items.descriptionMd: Store the token's hash and its expiry. A used or expired token shows a friendly page with a button to ask for a new link.

items.title: Plan comparison table
items.descriptionMd: Three columns, one per plan, with the current plan highlighted.

items.title: Toggle between monthly and annual prices
items.descriptionMd: Finance decided to keep annual pricing off the page for now; annual plans stay sales-led.

items.title: Download an invoice as a PDF
items.descriptionMd: Generate the PDF on request and cache it for a day.

items.title: Seat count meter in workspace settings
items.descriptionMd: Show how many active members the workspace has this month and what that will cost.

items.title: Add a stacking-order token for the widget launcher
items.descriptionMd: Give the launcher its own `z-index` token, set below common consent banners, so the host page can override it.

items.title: Widget launcher covers the cookie banner on small screens
items.descriptionMd:
On screens narrower than 400 px the launcher button sits on top of the host page's cookie banner, so a visitor cannot press **Accept**.

### Steps

1. Open the demo page on a 375 px wide screen.
2. Wait for the cookie banner.
3. Try to press **Accept**.

Expected: the banner is usable. Actual: the launcher is in the way.

comments.body: Screenshot attached. Happens on the demo page and on two customer sites.
Confirmed. Our launcher uses `z-index: 2147483647`, which wins over everything.
Can we let the host page override it with a data attribute?
Yes, that's the plan in the subtask.

items.title: Sign-in fails when the email has a trailing space
items.descriptionMd: Pasting an email address from a spreadsheet often adds a trailing space, and sign-in then says the account does not exist. Trim the address before looking it up.

items.title: CSV export garbles names with accents
items.descriptionMd: Opening the export in a spreadsheet shows `Ã©` instead of `é` and drops emoji.

comments.body: Reported by three customers this week, all using the default spreadsheet app on their laptops.
This is the encoding problem the byte-order mark subtask fixes. Marking it as a duplicate.
Thanks, I'll point the customers at that one.

items.title: Renewal invoices sent and charged twice
items.descriptionMd:
## Summary

Between 02:10 and 04:55 UTC on 23 September, 312 customers on annual plans received two copies of the same renewal invoice by email, and 41 of them were charged twice. Every duplicate charge was refunded by 11:30 UTC the same day, and every affected customer received a personal apology from the billing team. No card data was exposed and no invoice was sent to the wrong customer.

## What happened

The renewal job runs nightly and walks every subscription whose period ends in the next 24 hours. For each one it creates an invoice, asks the payment provider to charge the saved card, and then sends the invoice email. On the night of the incident the payment provider was slow: its median response time rose from about 400 ms to just over 9 seconds for roughly two hours.

Our HTTP client gives up after 8 seconds. When it gave up, the renewal job treated the charge as failed and put the subscription back on the queue with a five-minute delay. The provider, however, had not failed. It was only slow, and in most cases it completed the charge a second or two after we stopped waiting. Five minutes later the job picked the subscription up again, found no successful charge recorded on our side, created a second invoice and charged the card a second time.

The second charge did not always go through. Many cards were declined by the issuing bank as a suspected duplicate, which is why 312 customers got two emails but only 41 were charged twice.

## Why it was not caught sooner

The job's dashboard counts invoices created and charges attempted. Both numbers were higher than usual, but a busy renewal night looks exactly like that, so nobody was paged. The alert we do have fires when the charge failure rate passes 5%, and from our side the failure rate looked normal: every timed-out request was retried and the retry usually succeeded.

The first signal was a customer email at 05:20 UTC asking why they had two invoices. The on-call engineer confirmed the pattern within ten minutes and paused the renewal job at 05:34 UTC.

## Root cause

The charge request carried no idempotency key. The payment provider supports one: if two requests arrive with the same key, the second returns the result of the first instead of charging again. We had planned to add it when the billing service was rewritten last spring, and the ticket was closed when the rewrite shipped, but the key was only added to one-off charges, not to renewals. Nothing tested the renewal path with a slow provider, so the gap stayed invisible.

A second, smaller cause is that the job decides a charge failed when it simply did not hear back. "No answer" and "declined" are different outcomes, and the job only has a branch for one of them.

## What we changed

1. Every charge request, renewal or not, now carries an idempotency key built from the subscription id and the billing period. A retry of the same renewal can no longer create a second charge.
2. A timed-out charge is now recorded as `unknown`, not `failed`. The job asks the provider for the charge's status before it tries again, and only retries when the provider says no charge exists.
3. The invoice email is sent only after the charge is confirmed, so an `unknown` charge no longer produces an email.
4. We added a test that runs the renewal job against a provider stub that answers after 10 seconds, and asserts exactly one charge and one email per subscription.

## What we are still doing

- An alert on duplicate invoices per subscription per period, which would have fired within minutes on the night.
- A review of every other job that calls the payment provider, to confirm each one sends an idempotency key. The export job and the seat-change job are next.
- A short write-up for the support team on how to recognise this pattern from customer emails, since that was our fastest signal.

## Timeline (UTC)

- 02:10 Provider latency starts rising; first timeouts in the renewal job.
- 02:15 First duplicate invoice created.
- 04:55 Provider latency returns to normal; last duplicate created.
- 05:20 First customer email about two invoices.
- 05:34 Renewal job paused by on-call.
- 07:00 Affected customers identified from the invoice table.
- 11:30 All 41 duplicate charges refunded.
- 15:00 Apology emails sent; renewal job resumed with the idempotency key in place.

comments.body: Idempotency key is live for renewals and one-off charges. The slow-provider test is in CI.
Postmortem reviewed with finance. Closing; the follow-ups are tracked separately.
